title: api: v2 request/response schema versioning + beta headers + backcompat shims
author: Aisha Patel
ci_status: pass (initial flaky streaming test failed, rerun passed)
description:
Motivation: We need a formal schema versioning story for API request/response changes (structured output, tool/function calling payloads, streaming framing) so that SDKs and downstream consumers can safely opt-in and we can deprecate old fields. This PR introduces an explicit API schema header (X-Redwood-API-Schema: v2) and a beta header (X-Redwood-API-Beta: structured-output) to gate non-breaking additions, plus a set of server-side backcompat shims that map legacy OpenAI-compatible payloads to the new v2 canonical shape.

Summary of changes:
- Add api/schema/versioning.go: core logic for header parsing, negotiation, and canonical JSON transformations.
- Streaming stability: streaming.go updates the framing layer to attach schema metadata to framed chunks, fixes a race where EOF could be emitted before final metadata; adds a short buffering window to ensure final metadata consistently arrives.
- OpenAI compatibility layer: go/pkg/openai_compat/adapter.go implements translation for chat/completions->v2, including function/tool calling field mappings and embedding old "choices" shapes into the new structured output envelope when the client does not opt-in.
- SDKs: python/redwood_sdk/openai_compat.py updated to send beta header by default in dev builds and to expose helper to opt-in/opt-out.
- Docs: added docs/api/migration-v2.md with migration steps, sample curl requests, and deprecation timeline.
- Tests: added internal/tests/test_schema_versioning.py with unit coverage for header negotiation, shim correctness, and streaming final-chunk behavior.

Checklist:
- [x] Header negotiation & canonicalizer implemented
- [x] Backcompat shims for OpenAI-compat layer
- [x] Streaming final-metadata reliability improved + tests
- [x] Migration docs + SDK helpers
- [x] Canary rollout config (deploy/feature-flags/v2-schema.yaml)

Rollout plan:
1) Merge feature branch behind feature-flag (deploy/feature-flags/v2-schema.yaml).
2) Enable on staging and run e2e + streaming canary for 48h.
3) Enable beta header by default in SDK dev builds and surface opt-in docs.
4) Monitor structured-output error rate and token/regression metrics for 7 days.
5) Gradual ramp to 25% production traffic, then 100% with deprecation notice for legacy fields 90 days after GA.

Notes for reviewers: this PR intentionally keeps the default behavior backward-compatible (no behavior change when no schema header is present). To opt into v2, callers must include the X-Redwood-API-Schema: v2 header; beta experiments can be enabled with X-Redwood-API-Beta: structured-output. The OpenAI compatibility adapter continues to accept legacy shapes and rewrites them server-side to avoid breaking existing clients during the rollout.
